decisions.reason: SOL loses the image of the last breath dispersing; the source says it scattered.
SOL keeps the meaning and makes the accumulated ages more idiomatic.
The source specifically uses the Dragon’s body as kindling; BASE preserves that image.
The pronoun clearly refers to the roar’s shock wave, keeping the source’s meaning.
The self-correction “no, their former comrades” preserves the source’s explicit correction.
The participial phrasing preserves the source’s parallel fragment and sense.
“Solitary” is not in the source; SOL keeps the groan without that added implication.
The emphatic restatement preserves the certainty that Morgoth was dead.
“Responded quickly enough” keeps the sense that their reaction came too late.
SOL preserves that the two recognized the phenomenon first and most clearly.
The source describes his vacant voice; SOL changes that vocal detail into being in a daze.
“But he hadn’t” naturally clarifies that the Undead King had not given up.
SOL keeps the warmth reaching his fingertips while avoiding the awkward phrasing.
SOL adds italics and shifts the line into a direct thought not marked in the source.
SOL preserves both characters turning away and reads naturally.
The source says three written characters, not three syllables; SOL avoids BASE’s factual error.
“Never reached” makes the failure absolute; the source says the beep had not reached its owner.
SOL naturally conveys that the changes themselves were dramatic.
The source compares the changes to a marauder; SOL changes the singular image to plural marauders.
The source explicitly calls the chaos a pit; SOL drops that image.
“Unfolding” keeps the meaning and reads naturally in the description.
SOL turns the fragment into a clear sentence without changing the pillar’s description.
SOL preserves the paradox of a blinding beam associated with darkness in natural English.
“A world gone quiet” naturally retains the source’s silence.
SOL preserves the catastrophe blooming and scattering spores while improving the sentence flow.
Addressing the subordinate as “you’re calling that” fits the rebuke and keeps its meaning.
The source’s reference to a Mutation Gate’s occurrence is preserved by the natural recast.
SOL says the Gates become Monster Waves; the source says they reach a level where they can progress into them.
“A sudden ringing” preserves the sudden onset without changing the event.
“One place and one place only” keeps the exclusive destination and the direct-line emphasis.
SOL preserves the tremor in the recipient’s voice with natural phrasing.
SOL cleanly connects the people who understood Code Black to the preceding claim.
The typographic apostrophe changes no meaning.
“Two hundred or so” accurately conveys the source’s approximate quantity.
“Seasoned political instincts” preserves the source’s experienced political acumen without BASE’s added battle-hardened implication.
The source says his face’s injuries had not healed; “still wounded” does not preserve that detail as clearly.
SOL specifies that his grandfather’s name was recorded, which the source does not say.
SOL naturally preserves the sense that this place seemed to belong to someone else.
